verdicts.evidence: Removing .sort() makes the 'deterministic inventory' depend on readdir order, which Node leaves unspecified. Measured on a fixture rules directory where APFS's UTF-8 byte order differs from JS code-unit order (astral-plane vs BMP filenames): readRuleSet returned slugs in a different order than pristine. On the shipped corpus this filesystem happens to return sorted order, so smoke's sortedness assertion and every other layer stayed green. Re-measured 2026-11-10 (mutation-ratchet.yml run 42807518226, mode=measure, at 7d1846b): Stryker reported it Killed only because test/unit/example-packed.test.js refused the tarball npm packed inside Stryker's sandbox (`tar -xzf`, members under package/../../node_modules), a failure independent of the mutant, while every other covering test passed; re-run alone on that test on 2026-11-13 against a local build byte-identical to the measured source, it survives, so this filing stands.
